subject: Request: SLA exception for content-filter tool-calls affecting transaction confirmations
messages:
From: Oliver Hayes <oliver.hayes@omnipay.com>
To: priyom.das@redwood.com
Cc: procure@omnipay.com, security@omnipay.com
Date: Mon, 02 May 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Request: SLA exception for content-filter tool-calls affecting transaction confirmations

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We started a small pilot with Redwood last month and have run into a recurring issue that impacts our transaction confirmation flow. In brief: when Redwood's content-filter chain invokes tool-calls for structured output validation, we've seen sporadic timeouts and transformation failures that cause our payment confirmations to be delayed or returned with malformed JSON.

We understand filters are important for compliance, but these failures are happening ~0.6% of the time during peak windows and our ops team is seeing a material increase in "confirmation retry" footnotes. Because confirmation latency is a user-impacting metric, we need to propose a narrow SLA carve-out and fallback behavior while we stabilize. Specifically, please provide:

- A proposed amendment (language we can push to procurement) that outlines an exception when filter/tool-call failures cause downstream structured-output corruption;
- Concrete SLOs for filter/tool-calls (p95 latency, timeout definitions) and a commitment to mitigation timelines;
- Any logs you can share for the incidents (we've attached a sample call log).

We'd prefer a short-term operational mitigation (allow-through with flag + audit tag) plus a credit/remediation mechanism rather than full service credit if Redwood can guarantee a patch timeline. Can you confirm next steps and whether Redwood can operate under a temporary exception while the root cause is addressed?

--Oliver
Oliver Hayes
Head of Security & Infrastructure
Omnipay

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 03 May 2027 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Request: SLA exception for content-filter tool-calls affecting transaction confirmations

Team — forwarding Omnipay's note (below). Key asks: narrow contractual exception, an operational fallback (allow-through+tag), telemetry/export of failed transform counts, and a remediation SLA.

My suggested bullet points for the SLA amendment (draft for legal):
1) Scope: Exception applies only when a staffed filter/tool-call chain (stateless validators & third-party tools) returns malformed or timed-out structured output that causes user-visible transaction confirmation failure.
2) Operational fallback: During the exception window, Redwood will provide a configurable "tag-and-pass" mode that preserves the original model output and annotates the event for Omnipay to ingest; the tagged output must be delivered within the standard response window (no synthetic retry introduced).
3) Latency carve-out: A defined filter/tool-call timeout (default 750ms) will not count toward the 95% response-time SLO for the primary generation endpoint if the tag-and-pass fallback is enabled and Omnipay acknowledges receipt.
4) Credit/remediation: If malformed confirmations caused by filter/tool-call failures exceed 0.5% of confirmed transactions in any billing month, Redwood will issue a proportional credit and provide a remediation timeline (P1 patch within 10 business days).
5) Monitoring: Redwood will share a daily failed-transform export and provide an escalation contact and runbook.

Marcus — can you validate whether tag-and-pass is achievable as a config parameter in the next 48 hours and whether 750ms is a reasonable default timeout? If we can commit to a pilot of 30 days with daily exports, Legal can push a short amendment.

Thanks,
Priyom

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Request: SLA exception for content-filter tool-calls affecting transaction confirmations — proposed amendment and pilot plan

Oliver — thanks for the patience. Below is a consolidated response and a proposed short-term path to limit customer impact while we root-cause the failures. Attached is a draft SLA amendment and a short operational playbook.

Summary (high level):
- We can support a time-limited exception with an opt-in tag-and-pass fallback while Product implements a permanent fix.
- Proposed default timeout for filter/tool-calls: 750ms (configurable per-route). If the fallback is enabled and the event is tagged & delivered, the primary-generation SLO will exclude the filter/tool-call delay for that request.
- Credit mechanics: If malformed confirmations attributable to filter/tool-call failures exceed 0.5% of confirmed transactions in any billing month, Redwood will issue a credit equal to 25% of that month’s hosting charges for affected routes (subject to verification).
- Remediation commitment: P1 investigation within 24 hours of detection; patch window target 10 business days for regressions caused by Redwood code paths (third-party tool failures will follow the vendor escalation path but Redwood will coordinate).
- Telemetry & runbook: We will provide a daily failed-transform CSV export to your S3/GDrive location and a Slack escalation channel (crowd-managed).

Next steps we propose:
1) 30-day pilot with tag-and-pass enabled on the pilot routes (you opt in) — Redwood provides daily exports and a dedicated escalation engineer.
2) Legal to review the attached amendment and propose minor edits. If agreeable, we can route for signature (DocuSign link included).
3) Weekly checkpoint (15 min) during the pilot to review telemetry and tune the timeout/config.

Attachments (attached to this thread):
- redwood-sla-amendment-draft.pdf (proposed contract language)
- omnipay_sla_amendment_request.pdf (your original ask)
- filter_call_log_20270502.csv (samples you provided, correlated with preliminary telemetry)

Links: DocuSign: DocuSign: 0a9b1c-omnipay-sla-amend; Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/omnipay-sla-refs

If this looks acceptable, happy to schedule the kickoff for Thursday at 10:30 PT and loop in our on-call engineer.
